# Copilot Instructions for Data Analytics Slides Project

## Project Overview
This is a Slidev-based presentation project for data analytics education. It contains educational slides about data analysis, databases, spreadsheets, data visualization, and research methods. These slides are being used in the VCE Applied Computing: Data Analytics course.

## Technology Stack
- **Slidev**: Vue-powered presentation framework
- **Vue 3**: Frontend framework 
- **UnoCSS**: Atomic CSS framework for styling
- **Markdown**: Content format for slides
- **TypeScript**: For components and theme customization

## Project Structure
```
da-slides/
├── slides.md                    # Main slide deck entry point
├── pages/                       # Individual slide modules
├── components/                  # Vue components
├── layouts/                     # Custom layouts
├── theme/                       # Custom theme files
├── public/img/                  # Static images
├── styles.css                   # GM Default tokens and component styles
└── package.json                 # Dependencies and scripts
```

## Content Guidelines

### Slide Content
- Focus on data analytics education topics
- Wherever possible reference the VCE Applied Computing Study Design
- Refer to VCE Applied Computing: Data Analytics for relevant content
- Keep content clear and beginner-friendly
- Use bullet points and concise explanations
- Include practical examples and activities
- Add exam questions and marking criteria when relevant

### Markdown Conventions
- Use frontmatter for slide configuration:
  ```yaml
  ---
  layout: center
  transition: fade
  hideInToc: false
  title: Slide Title
  ---
  ```
- Use `##` for slide sections, `#` for main headings
- Bold important terms with `**text**`
- Use `<div class="callout">` for highlighted content boxes (`<div class="callout-important">` for must-not-miss information)

### Layout Usage
- `layout: cover` - Title slides
- `layout: center` - Content slides
- `layout: two-cols-header` - Two-column content
- `layout: default` - Standard layout
- `layout: li` - Learning intentions and success criteria. Should have `::li::` and `::sc::` for learning intentions and success criteria respectively.

## Styling Guidelines

All styling follows the **GM Default** design system (navy for identity, cool greys for structure, tints rather than borders for hierarchy). Tokens and component classes live in `styles.css`; heading scale and layout rules live in `theme/styles/layouts.css`.

### Principles
- **Restraint:** one strong visual moment per slide; keep everything else quiet.
- **Tints before borders:** group content with `surface-tint` panels. Save borders for the important callout.
- **Accessible by default:** every text colour pairing meets 4.5:1 contrast in light and dark mode.
- Labels are short and in **sentence case**. Never use all caps.

### Colour tokens
Use the CSS variables, never hard-coded colours or Tailwind/UnoCSS colour utilities (`bg-green-300`, `text-indigo-600`, etc.). Dark mode values switch automatically under `html.dark`.

| Variable | Light | Dark | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-navy` | #1e3a5f | #1e3a5f | Identity colour |
| `--gm-surface` | #ffffff | #1e3a5f | Slide background |
| `--gm-surface-tint` | #f1f5f9 | #2d4570 | Callouts, panels, table headers |
| `--gm-heading` | #1e3a5f | #ffffff | Headings, bold text, links |
| `--gm-ink` | #1f2937 | #f1f5f9 | Body text |
| `--gm-text-secondary` | #5f6875 | #cbd5e1 | Captions, labels, subtitles, footer |
| `--gm-accent` | #5b6b80 | #aeb9ca | Important callout border, italic emphasis, icons |
| `--gm-border` | #9ca3af | #94a3b8 | Decorative dividers only (never text or control borders) |

Spacing: `--gm-space-1|2|3|4|6|8|12|16` (4 to 64px; 24px `--gm-space-6` is the base rhythm and callout padding). Radius: `--gm-radius-sm` 4px, `--gm-radius-md` 8px (cards, callouts), `--gm-radius-full` (pills).

### Typography
- Fonts are set in `slides.md` frontmatter (`sans: Public Sans,Outfit`, `mono: Source Code Pro`).
- **Headings:** Outfit 600, letter spacing -0.5px, line height 1.2, `--gm-heading` colour. Scale: cover/intro h1 48px, h1 36px, h2 28px, h3 22px.
- **Body:** Public Sans 400, line height 1.6. Small text 14px; labels 12px weight 600 (`h6` and `.callout-label` use the label style).
- Emphasise with soft tinted fills, not extra sizes. These fills are a project-specific addition to GM Default (tokens `--gm-mark-*`, muted dark versions in dark mode):
  - `**bold**` renders bold navy on soft green (`--gm-mark-strong`)
  - `*italic*` renders italic on soft rose (`--gm-mark-em`)
  - `***bold italic***` renders on soft amber (`--gm-mark-em-strong`)
  - links render navy and underlined on soft orange (`--gm-mark-link`)
  - Emphasis inside `h1`/`h2` has no fill
  - Use emphasis for key terms only; a slide full of fills loses the "one strong moment" rule

### Component classes
- `<div class="callout">` - **standard callout** for tips, notes, extensions and Study Design quotes: tinted background, no border. Use this for most highlighted content.
- `<div class="callout-important">` - **important callout** for information students must not miss: 2px double `--gm-accent` border, no tint. Use sparingly.
- `<div class="note">` - legacy alias of `.callout`; existing slides use it, prefer `.callout` in new content.
- `<span class="callout-label">` - small sentence-case label above a callout heading.
- `.col-left` / `.col-right` - tinted column panels.
- `.text-secondary` - secondary text colour.
- Tables get a tinted header row and thin decorative dividers automatically.
- Leave a blank line after the opening `<div>` so Markdown inside it renders.

### What not to do
- No thick left borders on cards or callouts.
- No all-caps labels or `uppercase` utilities.
- No mixing of border styles on one component.
- No decorative shadows or gradients.
- No `opacity` to fade text (it breaks contrast); use `--gm-text-secondary`.
- No more than one strong visual moment per slide.

## Component Development
- Create Vue components in `/components/` directory
- Use simple, educational-focused components
- Follow Vue 3 Composition API patterns
- Keep components reusable across slides

## Content Creation Best Practices

### Educational Content
- Start with clear learning objectives
- Provide step-by-step explanations
- Include practical activities and exercises
- Add "Your Turn" sections for student engagement
- Reference real exam questions and marking criteria

### Data Analytics Topics
- Cover core concepts: databases, spreadsheets, visualization
- Include consent and ethical considerations
- Provide practical examples and case studies
- Connect theory to real-world applications

### Slide Design
- Use consistent layouts and styling
- Include relevant images in `/public/img/`
- Keep text readable with appropriate font sizes
- Use the GM Default tokens and callout classes rather than ad hoc colours

## Development Workflow
- Run `npm run dev` for local development
- Test slides in presentation mode
- Use `npm run build` for production builds
- Export to PDF with `npm run export`

## Code Style
- Use meaningful file names for slide modules
- Keep individual slide files focused on single topics
- Comment complex Vue components
- Use TypeScript for type safety where applicable

## Content Maintenance
- Update exam questions to current years
- Refresh examples and case studies regularly
- Ensure accessibility compliance
- Test all interactive elements

## When Adding New Content
1. Create new `.md` files in `/pages/` directory
2. Add to main `slides.md` with `src:` directive
3. Use appropriate layouts and styling
4. Include practical activities where relevant
5. Test in both light and dark modes

Remember: This is an educational resource focused on making data analytics concepts accessible to students. Prioritize clarity, engagement, and practical application in all content creation.
